Budget Plan for Advanced Hiking Gear

Initial Costs (One-time Investment)

1. High-Quality Hiking Boots
   - Estimated Cost: $150 - $250
   - Rationale: Essential for challenging trails, providing ankle support and durability.

2. Durable Backpack (50-70L for multi-day treks)
   - Estimated Cost: $200 - $400
   - Rationale: Needs to be lightweight yet strong enough to carry gear for several days.

3. Lightweight Tent (2-3 person capacity)
   - Estimated Cost: $200 - $350
   - Rationale: Must be weather-resistant and easy to set up for multi-day use.

Total Initial Investment: $550 - $1,000

Ongoing Costs (Annual/Multi-year)

1. Gear Maintenance and Replacement
   - Boot Resoling/Replacement: $50 - $100 every 2-3 years
   - Backpack Repair/Replacement: $50 - $100 every 5-7 years
   - Tent Repair/Replacement: $50 - $100 every 5-7 years
   - Estimated Annual Average: $30 - $50

2. Trail Fees and Permits
   - Varies by location; average $10 - $30 per trip
   - Estimated Annual Cost (assuming 10 trips): $100 - $300

3. Consumables (Food, Fuel, etc.)
   - Not directly gear-related but part of hiking budget
   - Estimated Annual Cost: $200 - $500

Total Annual Ongoing Cost: $330 - $850

Summary

- Initial Investment: $550 - $1,000
- Annual Ongoing Cost: $330 - $850

This budget allows Alex to invest in high-quality gear that will last for years while accounting for regular maintenance and trail-related expenses.
